 SALT LAKE CITY (KUTV) — Two product recalls announced by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission include Pamag Pieeoo mattresses that may not meet federal flammability standards and NTI and HTP gas boilers that could pose fire, carbon monoxide and impact hazards.
 The Pamag Pieeoo twin-XL mattresses were sold online at Amazon.com in March 2026 for between $80 and $95. The eight-inch mattresses have a white top and sides with a gray curve pattern. The model number, BFC8HMBYTX-US, is printed on a label sewn into one side.
 The CPSC says the mattresses violate the mandatory flammability standard, posing a risk of serious injury or death in a fire. Consumers should stop using the mattresses and contact Longjili Trading for a full refund. The company will ask consumers to write “RECALLED” on the mattress, send a photo to Pamagpieeoo@outlook.com, then dispose of it. No injuries have been reported.

 The NTI and HTP residential gas boilers were sold nationwide through independent heating and plumbing contractors and wholesale distributors from May 2021 through July 2026. They cost between $3,200 and $7,700. The recalled models include NTI’s FTVN and TFTN series and HTP’s EFTU series. The model and serial number are on the rating plate on the left side of the boiler.
 The CPSC says a condensate dish inside the boiler can crack during delayed ignition, allowing gas to build up. If that gas ignites, the boiler’s front cover could detach, creating fire, carbon monoxide poisoning and impact hazards. The agency says the company has received 34 reports of the dish breaking, including three reports of the cover detaching. One technician reportedly suffered a broken jaw.
 Consumers should stop using the recalled boilers and contact Ariston to schedule a free repair by a certified technician. Anyone who must continue using a boiler while waiting for repair should make sure working smoke and carbon monoxide alarms are installed in the home. Contact Ariston at 800-688-2575, email VCexchanger@ariston.com, or visit the NTI or HTP recall websites.
